gaps.sentence: I'm afraid we're ___ of options at this point.
The climbers were well ___ of schedule by midday.
Everything was packed ready in ___ of the movers' arrival.
The soldiers were ___ of danger once they had crossed the river.
gaps.explanation: 'Out of danger' = no longer at risk.

gaps.sentence: ___ good fortune, nobody was hurt in the collapse.
gaps.explanation: 'through good fortune' = by means of luck.

gaps.sentence: He stayed ___ touch with every colleague he'd ever had.
He acted on his own ___ and did not ask permission.
gaps.hint: on your own ___ = without being told
gaps.explanation: 'On one's own initiative' = deciding and acting independently.

gaps.sentence: ___ reference to your letter of 12 May, we are still processing the claim.
gaps.explanation: 'With reference to' introduces the subject of a formal letter.
